content:
We've built a new CI setup for Mathlib, that removes the need for contributors to make PRs from branches pushed directly to the leanprover-community/mathlib4 repository, and instead allows making PRs from forks (i.e. per the usual practice for any git repository).

In particular, we will be removing write access to the repository from most users.
Discussion thread at #mathlib4 > all future PRs should be made from forks .

An update on this: mathlib will be fully moving to the standard "PR from fork" model on this Wednesday, 18th June. On this date, write access to non-master branches of mathlib will be removed from all contributors other than a small subset of maintainers.

It is already not possible to create a new PR from a branch. For those unsure about the workflow, please read any explanation on the internet about how to contribute to an open source project; our workflow is now standard and no longer mathlib-specific.

For those who already have PRs in progress from branches, there is no need to hurry. You will be unable to make any further commits to those PRs, but the work and reviews are not lost. The workflow to get things up and running again is the following. The manual approach: close the PR, open a new PR from a fork with the same content (i.e. from the same branch but this time on your fork), and write a comment on the fork PR linking to the branch PR. Mathlib also offers a migration workflow script; it is in scripts/migrate_to_fork.py in mathlib; this should do the work for you in a step-by-step way and will also copy all of the comments from the old PR to the new one. Note that the migration workflow script will still work fine at any point, you do not have to migrate everything by Wednesday.

Any discussion or questions regarding this message should take place in the discussion thread linked to above: #mathlib4 > all future PRs should be made from forks .
